newsitem.title: INDIA: India says health insurance sector opened.
newsitem.headline: India says health insurance sector opened.

text.p: India said on Friday that it was opening its health insurance sector by allowing state firms to launch joint ventures.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, while presenting the budget 1997/98 (April-March), said the state-owned General Insurance Corporation would be allowed to have selected Indian companies as joint venture partners in the health insurance sector.
Chidambaram said the insurance company would be allowed to determine the terms and conditions of services of its agents and employees.
India began liberalising trade, industry and banking in 1991 as part of a sweeping economic liberalisation programme, dismantling decades of socialist controls.
At present all Indian insurance companies are state-owned.
